name: Wasmer

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Includes the same 6 active CPU-hours, 400 GB-hours RAM, 150 GB bandwidth, 1 GB volume/package storage, 1M requests and 1,000 build minutes as Hobby; overages $0.10/CPU-h, $0.01/GB-h RAM, $0.10/GB egress, $0.05/GB storage, $0.50/M requests, $0.005/build-min, $0.25/app after 100, $0.01/domain after 50, $0.001/email; database $0.01/MB; one daily backup then $0.20/backup.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Free forever; 1 member, 100 apps, 500 deploys/month, 1M requests, 150 GB bandwidth, 6 active CPU-hours, 400 GB-hours memory, 1 GB volume and package storage, 100 MB database per app, 1,000 build minutes, 50 custom domains; low execution priority; no SSH/SFTP.

caveats: Wasmer WebAssembly execution is not a full Linux VM; card isolation isolate is approximate because engine lacks wasm enum. Pricing uses active CPU plus provisioned memory.

Pro includes separate 6 active CPU-hours, 400 GB-hours memory, 150 GB bandwidth, 1 GB volume and package storage, 1M requests and 1000 build-minutes. These category-specific allowances cannot be collapsed into fully fungible credits.
Pro $10/mo; extra seats $5, app beyond 100 $0.25, requests $0.50/M, builds $0.005/min, volumes/packages $0.05/GB-month; databases and backups separate.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: one of the features on our roadmap is persistent instances, which will keep running, and won't be dynamically spawned or terminated
snapshot_auto.note: Instances are ephemeral (terminated after a few idle minutes or evicted); nothing saves an instance's state at stop. InstaBoot is automatic but different: Edge warms up a fresh instance, snapshots it (journal+memory) per app version and boots new instances from that snapshot; it does not carry a stopped instance's state forward. Durable state only via volumes/databases.

guest_firewall.note: Workloads are WebAssembly/WASIX instances on the Wasmer runtime, not a Linux VM or container: there is no guest kernel netfilter, so nftables/iptables cannot run.

secret_proxy.quote: You can manage secure environment variables - from now on simply _secrets_ -
secret_proxy.note: App secrets are environment variables injected into the app (CLI wasmer app secrets create/list/reveal/update/delete, or dashboard); no injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes provide persistent disk storage for applications.
volume_attach.note: Declared in app.yaml (name + mount path), multiple per app, single region only; also S3-API remote access and SFTP. $0.05/GB-month on pricing page.

volume_shared.quote: Keep in mind that volumes can be accessed concurrently, and even from different nodes.
volume_shared.note: Read-write-many ('volumes at the moment only provide *read-write-many* semantics'); all auto-scaled instances of an app share them, including across nodes in the one region. Not recommended for single-writer databases.

isolation.quote: WebAssembly enables secure, sandboxed execution of untrusted code, without the burden of additional emulation layers like containers or virtual machines.
isolation.note: Apps run as compiled WASM/WASIX packages on Wasmer's own runtime, not in Linux containers or VMs.

image_oci.quote: Each app is based on a package from the registry, which is then deployed to the Wasmer Edge cloud.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — apps are built from Wasm packages published to the Wasmer Registry, not from Docker/OCI images.

docker_inside.quote: Wasmer Edge does not inherit the technical debt and constraints of other hypervisor and virtualization platforms such as virtual machines and Kubernetes as it builds up a full virtualized and sand-boxed layer built on the WASM runtime itself
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the runtime is a WASM/WASIX sandbox with no container engine or Docker daemon inside it.

nested_virt.quote: a full virtualized and sand-boxed layer built on the WASM runtime itself with minimal complexity
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a WASM instance has no /dev/kvm or hypervisor access.

desktop.quote: Find the perfect plan for your project ... Deploy Git repositories on Wasmer Edge
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Wasmer Edge hosts stateless HTTP apps/WordPress/static sites, not a graphical desktop.

browser.quote: Find the perfect plan for your project
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no managed/real browser product.

computer_use.quote: Find the perfect plan for your project
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no desktop to drive by screenshots/clicks.

anti_bot.quote: Find the perfect plan for your project
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Wasmer Edge is a WASM app-hosting PaaS, not a browser/scraping product.

captcha_solving.quote: Find the perfect plan for your project
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: us-hillsboro, us-ashburn, us-losa1, ca-beau1, fr-roub1, de-falkenstein
egress_ip_type.note: Edge nodes run in standard commercial datacenters; no residential/mobile IP product offered.

snapshot.quote: InstaBoot allows fast startup by creating a snapshot of your app that is fully initialized and ready to serve requests.
snapshot.note: InstaBoot snapshots are an automatic, per-app-version boot-speed optimization (memory+journal warm-up), not a user-invoked snapshot/restore of a specific running instance's state. Instances themselves are stateless/ephemeral; durable state only via volumes/databases.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots are created by starting a new application instance and warming it up with a series of warm-up requests.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Snapshotting is InstaBoot's automatic warm-up mechanism triggered by deployment, not an on-demand API/CLI checkpoint of a running instance.

fork.quote: App instances are currently stateless and ephemeral. They will automatically be started to serve requests, and shut down again after a short idle period.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no clone-a-machine primitive; new instances are auto-spawned from the app package, not forked from a running instance.

fork_running.quote: App instances are currently stateless and ephemeral.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: App instances are currently stateless and ephemeral.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no forking primitive at all.

persistent_disk.quote: Volumes provide persistent disk storage for applications.
persistent_disk.note: App instances themselves are ephemeral, but attached Volumes persist across deploys/restarts.

auto_stop_idle.quote: They will automatically be started to serve requests, and shut down again after a short idle period.

live_resize.quote: Active CPU ... 6 hours (then $0.10 per active CPU hour) ... Provisioned Memory ... 400 GB-hours (then $0.01 per GB-hour)
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a serverless auto-scaled model with no user-controlled CPU/RAM sizing of a running instance was found.

agent_harnesses.quote: Deploy Git repositories on Wasmer Edge
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Wasmer Edge is a web-app/WordPress/static-site hosting PaaS; no coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) templates found.

harness_api.quote: Deploy Git repositories on Wasmer Edge
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

own_agent_api.quote: Deploy Git repositories on Wasmer Edge
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent product.

lang_python.quote: Python Deployments: Run Python applications using WebAssembly containers.
lang_python.note: Also has a dedicated 'Python Flask Server' guide and a py2wasm Python-to-Wasm compiler.

public_ipv4.note: Dedicated IPv4 is a paid add-on on Pro (1 included, then $1/IP) and available on Enterprise; not included on free Hobby.

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Wasmer Edge pricing/plans only cover CPU and memory; no GPU instance type found.

arm64.quote: Wasmer Edge abstracts regions away for most stateless applications; the platform will route requests to the closest healthy region automatically.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Edge is a WASM PaaS with no selectable machine/CPU architecture (Wasm bytecode itself is architecture-neutral, compiled by the host runtime); no ARM machine type is offered to choose.

eu_data_residency.quote: fr-roub1 France Roubaix ... de-falkenstein Germany Falkenstein
eu_data_residency.note: Apps (and databases/volumes for fr-roub1) can be pinned to EU regions via locality.regions in app.yaml.

windows.quote: Run your apps in lightweight WebAssembly sandboxes: locally or on our cloud. Deploy and scale apps and AI agents on Wasmer Edge.
windows.note: Wasmer Edge runs apps as WebAssembly/WASIX instances on the Wasmer runtime, not as guest VMs with a selectable OS; there is no Windows guest offering. Windows for this WASM sandbox product is outside what the product is, same as the card's edge mode os:["linux"].

macos.quote: Run your apps in lightweight WebAssembly sandboxes: locally or on our cloud. Deploy and scale apps and AI agents on Wasmer Edge.
macos.note: Same reasoning as windows: Wasmer Edge executes WebAssembly/WASIX modules, not full guest operating systems, so there is no macOS guest offering.

ingress_rules.quote: kind, name, package, env, cli_args, debug, redirect, capabilities (instaboot, cdn_cache, ssh, database), health_checks, locality, scaling, jobs
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the full app.yaml schema and Edge docs expose no IP allowlist / private-URL / security-group style control over who can reach an app's exposed HTTP port; apps are reachable via their public *.wasmer.app / custom-domain URL to anyone.

egress_allowlist.quote: Wasmer Edge uses a virtual networking overlay exposed directly to the WASIX sandbox... we will continue to unlock more core networking functionality.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress control is documented anywhere in the app.yaml config or architecture docs; outbound networking is plain POSIX sockets via the WASIX sandbox.

egress_http_rules.quote: kind, name, package, env, cli_args, debug, redirect, capabilities, health_checks, locality, scaling, jobs
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no HTTP method/path-level egress rule mechanism is documented; same evidence as egress_allowlist.

static_egress_ip.note: The only fixed-IP feature documented is a paid 'Dedicated IP' add-on, which is an inbound public IPv4 for reaching the app, not a fixed outbound/egress IP; no static egress IP is mentioned anywhere in the docs or pricing pages.

byoc.quote: Enterprise & Subhosting ... All in Pro plan plus: Unlimited users, Subhosting, Private dedicated locations, 99.95% SLA, Compliance, Advanced support
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Enterprise offers 'private dedicated locations' within Wasmer's own multi-tenant Edge network (and 'subhosting' for reselling), not deployment of the managed service into a customer-owned cloud account; no BYOC/VPC-deploy offering is documented.

usage_api.quote: Wasmer Edge pricing is tracked through the dashboard and invoices based on active CPU hours, GB-hours of memory, bandwidth, and storage, but no public API endpoint exists for querying billable usage of individual apps or deployments.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; The Wasmer GraphQL API at registry.wasmer.io/graphql is for package discovery and registry queries only, not for usage metrics. The wasmer CLI provides app management commands (wasmer app info, wasmer app list) but no usage/billing endpoints. Usage visibility appears limited to account-level invoices and dashboard UI.
